questions.problem:
Let $(x,y)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $x-y?$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.04x-0.08y-4=0 \\ 2x-3y=4\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the top equation by $100,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.04x-0.08y-4=0 & |\,\times 100 \\ 2x-3y=4 & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}4x-8y-400=0 \\ 2x-3y=4\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we multiply the second equation by $-2,$ we will get a $-4x$ term in the second equation that can cancel with the $4x$ term in the first equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x-8y-400=0 &  \\ 2x-3y=4 & |\,\times (-2)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}4x-8y-400=0 \\ -4x+6y=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{4x}-8y-400 & =0 \\ -\cancel{4x}+6y & =-8 \\ (-8y+6y)-400 & =-8 \\ -2y & =392 \\ y & =-196\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $y=-196$ into the equation $2x-3y=4$ to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-3y & =4 \\ 2x-3(-196) & =4 \\ 2x+588 & =4 \\ 2x & =-584 \\ x & =-292\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-292$ and $y=-196.$ So, 

$$
x-y=-292-(-196)=-292+196=-96.
$$

questions.problem:
Let $(x,y)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $x-y?$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2.3x+4.6y=69 \\ 10x-20y=100\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the top equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2.3x+4.6y=69 & |\,\times 10 \\ 10x-20y=100 & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}23x+46y=690 \\ 10x-20y=100\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we divide the first equation by $23$ and the second equation by $10,$ we will get a $2y$ term in the first equation that can cancel with the $-2y$ term in the second equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}23x+46y=690 & |\,÷23 \\ 10x-20y=100 & |\,÷10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}x+2y=30 \\ x-2y=10\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $y$-variable and allows us to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\cancel{2y} & =30 \\ x-\cancel{2y} & =10 \\ (x+x) & =(30+10) \\ 2x & =40 \\ x & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $x=20$ into the equation $x+2y=30$ to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y & =30 \\ (20)+2y & =30 \\ 2y & =30-20 \\ 2y & =10 \\ y & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=20$ and $y=5.$ So, 

$$
x-y=20-(5)=15.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the solution of the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.2p+0.3q=0.6 \\ 0.2p-0.1q=0.4\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $10,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.2p+0.3q=0.6 & |\times 10 \\ 0.2p-0.1q=0.4 & |\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2p+3q=6 \\ 2p-q=4\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the second equation by $-1,$ then we will get a $-2p$ term that can cancel with the $2p$ term in the first equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2p+3q=6 &  \\ 2p-q=4 & |\,\times (-1)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2p+3q=6 \\ -2p+q=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $p$-variable and allows us to solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{2p}+3q & =6 \\ -\cancel{2p}+q & =-4 \\ (3q+q) & =(6-4) \\ 4q & =2 \\ q & =\frac{2}{4} \\ q & =0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $q=0.5$ into the equation $2p-q=4$ to solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2p-q & =4 \\ 2p-0.5 & =4 \\ 2p & =4.5 \\ p & =\frac{4.5}{2} \\ p & =2.25\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $p=2.25,\,q=0.5.$

questions.problem:
Let $(x,y)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $x+y?$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.05x-0.03y=0.04 \\ 0.4x+0.2y=0.1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the first equations by $100$ and the second equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.05x-0.03y=0.04 & |\times 100 \\ 0.4x+0.2y=0.1 & |\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}5x-3y=4 \\ 4x+2y=1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $2$ and the second equation by $3,$ we will get a $-6y$ term in the first equation that can cancel with the $6y$ term in the second equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x-3y=4 & |\,\times (2) \\ 4x+2y=1 & |\,\times (3)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}10x-6y=8 \\ 12x+6y=3\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $y$-variable and allows us to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}10x-\cancel{6y} & =8 \\ 12x+\cancel{6y} & =3 \\ (10x+12x) & =(8+3) \\ 22x & =11 \\ x & =\frac{11}{22} \\ x & =0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $x=0.5$ into the equation $4x+2y=1$ to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+2y & =1 \\ 4(0.5)+2y & =1 \\ 2+2y & =1 \\ 2y & =-1 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ y & =-0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=0.5$ and $y=-0.5.$ So, 

$$
x+y=0.5+(-0.5)=0.
$$

Example: 
                    Solving a System Containing Decimals in Both Equations
canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}1.4x+2.8y=1.4 \\ 0.02x+0.01y=0.05\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the first equation by $10$ and the second equation by $100,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14221949/assets/5e8fbe9a6109fb1b4046645e38993449229ff9ea0d4634a22d98e65a38786c2f.svg)

To simplify the first equation, we divide by $14\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14221949/assets/f673f4aa7086390409fef5d20ae5d9da38d480a501f5b563e2ae0d915c8a00a5.svg)

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the first equation can easily be solved for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y & =1 \\ x & =1-2y\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can substitute $x=1-2y$ into the second equation and then solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y & =5 \\ 2(1-2y)+y & =5 \\ 2-4y+y & =5 \\ 2-3y & =5 \\ -3y & =3 \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $x,$ we substitute $y=-1$ back into $x=1-2y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =1-2y \\  & =1-2(-1) \\  & =1+2 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x =3$ and $y =-1$, which can be expressed as $(3, -1).$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Sometimes, we might have a system of equations with decimal coefficients, such as the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.2x+y=1 \\ 0.15x-0.04y=0.2\end{aligned}
$$

To make the system easier to solve, we turn it into a system involving integer coefficients only.

In general, we multiply each equation by $10,$ or $100,$ or $1000,$ etc. depending on how many decimal places we need to eliminate. In this particular instance:

- We need to eliminate one decimal place in the top equation, so we multiply by $10.$

- We need to eliminate two decimal places in the bottom equation, so we multiply by $100.$

So, we multiply the first equation by $10$ and the second equation by $100,$ as follows:

tutorials.content:
Sometimes, we might have a system of equations with decimal coefficients, such as the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.2x+y=1 \\ 0.15x-0.04y=0.2\end{aligned}
$$

To make the system easier to solve, we turn it into a system involving integer coefficients only.

In general, we multiply each equation by $10,$ or $100,$ or $1000,$ etc. depending on how many decimal places we need to eliminate. In this particular instance:

- We need to eliminate one decimal place in the top equation, so we multiply by $10.$

- We need to eliminate two decimal places in the bottom equation, so we multiply by $100.$

So, we multiply the first equation by $10$ and the second equation by $100,$ as follows:

From here, we can solve the system of equations using either substitution or elimination.
